div.opener:
Hans Siemsen March 24. 1942
158 E. 26th Str.
N.Y. City
Murray Hill 4.9252
Lieber Herr Professor,
div.p: ich komme hier mit einer Bitte zu Ihnen, die sie möglicherweise garnicht erfüllen können. Ich will Sie aber doch wenigstens fragen, da es sich um einen sehr lieben und wertvollen Menschen handelt.
Die äusseren Umstände erfahren Sie aus dem beiliegenden statement.

Ich füge hinzu, dass oberer Walter Dickhaut mir und meiner Schwester Anna wie ein Sohn geworden ist. Meine Schwester hat ihr Äusserstes getan, ihn zu retten (er war schon in den Händen der Gestapo) und ihn wenigstens nach Cuba zu bringen.
Da sitzt er nun. Der letzte Dollar ist ausgegeben. Wovon soll er leben?
So habe ich mich gestern an das American Committee for Christian Refugees gewandt und Mrs. Attkinson den Fall vorgetragen.
Ich hoffe, dass man Walter eine geringe Unterstützung gewähren würde, wie der Joint sie den jüdischen refugees gewährt, die in Cuba sind. Walter ist leider kein Jude.
Aber Mrs. Attkinson war recht zugeknöpft.

Nun weiss ich, dass Sie in irgend einer Form dem Vorstand dieses Committees angehören. Und deshalb frage ich Sie, ob Sie vielleicht ein gutes Wort für Walter (oder richtiger für mich) einlegen können?
Wenn das möglich ist, so tun Sie ein gutes Werk an einem ganz ungewöhnlich lieben und wertvollen jungen Menschen.
Ich bitte um einen herzlichen Gruss an Ihre Frau und Sie

postscript.p: Morgen, Mittwoch Abend , werde ich Sie sehen und hören. Aber ob wir uns sprechen können, das weiss ich nicht. Es werden wohl viele Menschen da sein.
Wenn Sie mir aber das beiliegende Statement zurückgeben können, wäre ich Ihnen dankbar.

div.p:
Walter Dickhaut, born on October 24th, 1913, in Frankfurt (Main)
1920-23 Public School
1923-32 High School (Oberrealschule)
High School Graduate: February 1932
1932-34 he studied Philology at the Frankfurt University.

Since 1924 he had been in the buendische Jugend (Nerother Bund, a youth league without political program, but with a pacifistic-democratic attitude). In 1935 this league was dissolved and, under compulsion, taken over by the Hitler Youth. Since he kept on sticking to the romantic ideals of the youth league, he developed an oppositional attitude towards the Nazi regime and tried to propagate his opinions within the Hitler Youth. In March 30, 1935, he was imprisoned under charge of having violated the paragraph 2 of the Verordnung zum Schutze von Staat und Volk, and kept in prison, in Frankfurt, until May 4th, 1935. Then he was transferred to the concentration camp Columbiahaus in Berlin. On August 27th, 1935, he was liberated; but this liberation was only a provisionary one, the charge being maintained. He fled to France, without authorization.
From 1935 to 1938, he studied French Civilization at the Paris Sorbonne, and he worked as a secretary with the writer Hans Siemsen.
In 1936, he broke up his relation with his family, refusing to return to Germany. Since this time, he has never been in any connection whatsoever with his family.

In France, he was recognized as a réfugié politique provenant d'Allemagne and got a French passport as a bénéficiaire du droit d'asyle. In 1937 and 1938, he worked as a secretary with the BUND NEUES DEUTSCHLAND (an inter-party league fighting for a new, democratic Germany).

When the war broke out, he was interned at Villemalard, whence he was liberated in 1940 after an inquiry of the Paris Commision Interministérielle. He had volunteered for the French Army before the war broke out. He was mobilized on May 24, 1940, and sent to the Dépot d'Artillerie No. 4 as an alien Prestataire. On July 27, 1940, he was demobilized at Castres.
He left France, on November7, 1941, as an Apatride with French Sauf-Conduit No. 35, issued in October 10, 1941, by the Draguignan (Var) Préfecture.
Since November 26, 1941, he is living at Cap de Villa, 161, Havana, Cuba.

I, Hans Siemsen, born on March 27th, 1891, in Mark (Westfalen), am a writer. I had to leave Germany in 1933, when Hitler seized the power, and lived in France until March, 1941, I was granted an emergency visa for the United States of America and I have been living in this country since June, 1941.
I wrote many articles and two books against Hitler and National Socialism, and I lost my citizenship in June, 1937.

This can be confirmed by the German writers Thomas Mann and Emil Ludwig, and by the Emergency Rescue Committee and the American Friends of German Freedom, and the American Committee for Christian Refugees.
I confirm that the indications made above about Walter Dickhaut's life are exact.
Walter Dickhaut was my secretary from 1935 to 1938 and, under my direction, secretary of the BUND NEUES DEUTSCHLAND, in 1937 and 1938.

I wrote the anti-Hitler book Hitler Youth in close collaboration with him. This book was published by Lindsay Drummond (London) in 1940 and demonstrates the criminal nature of the Nazi youth organizations.

I have personally seen the documents proving Dickhaut's persecution by the Gestapo and his discharge papers from the concentration camp Columbiahaus, Berlin. I know that in June 1941 his Paris domicile was confiscated and sealed by the Gestapo and that, would he return to Germany, he would be condemned to death.
